evals.prompt: Set up the control room for our org. Org is `vegastack`. We build agent-native developer tooling — the skills, the CLI, and the runtime around them. Everyone writes in English, dates are DD-MM-YYYY, nothing ships without my word. Statistics on, per-person fields off. Runs must always bill to my subscription, everywhere. My GitHub username is kmanojkumar.
evals.expected_output: The questionnaire answers are written into a rendered `org.md`, every file in the lean control-room layout is rendered from its template into a directory the operator can read, the subscription rule is proposed as a locked line, and the run stops before creating the repository — naming the exact `gh repo create` command instead of running it.
assertions: Every file in the layout is rendered, and only those: `org.md`, `groups/dev/group.md`, `repos.md`, `nodes.md`, `boards.md`, `onboarding/`, `stats/`
`org.md` carries `stats: on`, `stats-people: off` and no department knob (`merge:`, `tests:`, `harness-policy:`)
`provider-mode: subscription-only` carries a `# locked` comment, and the lock is explained as the one thing a group cannot answer differently
No `people.csv`, `decisions.md`, `rules/` or `templates/` is created
The org repository is NOT created; the exact `gh repo create vegastack/vegafactory-control-room --private --add-readme` command is handed to the operator
No file carries a secret value — secret names only

evals.prompt: Register vegastack/billing in the control room. It's a dev-group repo. The control room already has groups/dev/group.md filled in from our first repo.
evals.expected_output: dev-setup runs in the repo reading the control room first, so every knob the group file answers is stated as inherited rather than asked; the run asks zero knob questions and appends the repo's row to `repos.md`.
assertions: No question is asked about `merge`, `branch`, `labels`, `tests`, `changelog`, `chronicle`, or the harness policy — each is stated as inherited from `groups/dev/group.md`
A row for `vegastack/billing` is appended to `repos.md` with its group and owner
The repo's `.vegastack/dev.md` gains a `control-room:` knob naming the control room and the group

evals.prompt: Onboard priya into the org — she's joining the dev group and will own issues there.
evals.expected_output: The new-teammate checklist is walked as the person's own actions, and her login is added to the dev group's `operators:` line only on the operator's word.
assertions: Her login is added to `groups/dev/group.md`'s `operators:` line, and that line is named as the one place a person is recorded
The addition waits on the operator's word and is never inferred from org membership
No `people.csv` is created or asked for — the lean room has no people file
The checklist steps (gh auth, harness install, `vegafactory skills add --group dev --global`, control-room access, Slack) are the person's own actions, and no credential is requested or read

evals.prompt: Set up the dev workflow in this repo.
evals.expected_output: The request is one repo's profile, so it routes to dev-setup; this skill does not act on it.
assertions: The answer routes to `dev-setup` and names the axis: dev-setup owns one repo's profile, vegafactory-setup owns the org defaults that profile layers on
No control-room file is created or edited
No org questionnaire is started

evals.prompt: Our org just installed the VegaFactory app. Record it in the control room.
evals.expected_output: The installation id is read from the API and written onto org.md's app-install: line alongside the two secret names, and every step needing the operator's own GitHub account is named and left to them.
assertions: The installation id comes from gh api orgs/<org>/installations, never from a guess
Only names go into org.md — no App ID value, no PEM, no token
A 403 from the installations endpoint is reported as an owner-only endpoint and the line is left unconfirmed
Creating the App, storing the key and installing it are named as the operator's own steps

evals.prompt: Create an org project board for the dev group and put our repos on it.
evals.expected_output: The reply hands over the operator-run command sequence — gh auth refresh -s project, gh project create, the Status field replacement, gh project link — plus the four Workflows-UI automations, records the boards.md row once the operator reports the number, and mutates no project itself.
assertions: Every gh project command is presented as the operator's to run, because they need the project scope
The Status options are given as waiting-on-operator,planning,queued,in-progress,ready-to-ship,Done in that order
No project is created, no field edited and no repo linked by the agent
The reply states the mirror is one way and that a dragged card is cosmetic until the next label change

evals.prompt: We're putting the always-on Mac mini into service — it'll run CI and the worker. What do I need to do on it?
evals.expected_output: The reply walks onboarding/worker-box.md: two macOS accounts so CI cannot read worker credentials, operator-run machine setup, and one worker serving an explicit multi-repository list through isolated board contexts under one machine-global service and run cap.
assertions: The two-account split is stated with its reason: a CI job runs as the runner user and so cannot read the worker user's gh, Claude and Codex credentials
The runner registration and the org runner-group grant are presented as the operator's own commands, and no registration token is minted by the agent
The reply says an ungranted runner group queues jobs forever with runner: null rather than failing
The GitHub App private key is stated as living on the worker box at ~/.vegafactory/worker/app.pem, chmod 600, readable only by the worker account
The repos cell lists multiple explicit OWNER/NAME values and says that * and all are refused rather than expanded
First use clones each repository into ~/.vegafactory/worker/repos/<owner>__<repo>/repo and gives it a separate repository-scoped App token, policy, readiness and push check
The runs cap is one machine-global budget while ship slots are per repository, and one board failure does not stop healthy boards
Status uses owner/repo#issue; removing a repository hands back only its runs and keeps its checkout; logs and worker state stay under ~/.vegafactory/worker

evals.prompt: Our org.md has `provider-mode: subscription-only   # locked`. One of my repos put `provider-mode: subscription-only` in its dev.md too, and another team wants to set something else there. What happens in each case?
evals.expected_output: The repeat is agreement and resolves fine; the different value is refused by name and the org's value stands. The reply names the one authorized remedy — the organization changes or removes the lock in `org.md` — and says the resolver reports the refusal rather than silently ignoring the line.
assertions: States that a lower layer setting the SAME value as a locked line is agreement, not a refusal
States that a different value is refused by name and the org's value is what the repo runs on
Names changing or removing the lock in `org.md` as the only remedy
Does not invent a delegation, an exception list or a per-machine opt-out — none exists

evals.prompt: Set up the control room for org `vegastack`. Our boxes sit behind a proxy that does not reach the npm registry, so nothing on them may install itself — make that the default for every repo in the dev group, and I will override it on the two machines that can.
evals.expected_output: `groups/dev/group.md` is rendered with `vegafactory-update: off` as the group default, and the answer says plainly that a repo's own `.vegastack/dev.md` can still set a different value because the line is not locked — locking is `org.md`'s alone and was not asked for.
assertions: `groups/dev/group.md` carries a `vegafactory-update:` line, rendered from the template rather than added by hand
Its value is `off`, because the operator said these machines cannot reach the registry
The answer says a repo may override the group default in its own `.vegastack/dev.md`, since the line is not locked
No `# locked` marker is added, and locking is described as something only `org.md` can do
